page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.large is a memory-optimized instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the ARM64 architecture with Neoverse-V2 cores, the server features 2 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.8 GHz with one thread per core. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 118 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and network connectivity is rated at a baseline of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a mixture of average single-core capabilities and weaker multi-core performance. The instance achieves average ratings in stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores, alongside a strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 14.16 GB/sec. However, multi-core benchmarks such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core fall into the weak category. Passmark CPU scores are poor, particularly in encryption and extended instructions. Memory performance is average for large block read-only bandwidth and Passmark database operations, but weak for cached small block reads and large block writes.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r8gd.large offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio and built-in NVMe storage on an ARM-based architecture, which reduces resource overhead compared to x86 equivalents. However, the trade-off is limited compute scaling and lower multi-threaded throughput. This hardware profile is suited for memory-bound workloads with low parallel compute requirements, such as caching layers, lightweight database operations, and single-threaded data processing tasks that benefit from local SSD scratch space.
